note: Workflow Access (submodule of Workflow) controls node access per workflow state and role via core's node grant system (node-only). Per-state grants live in config workflow_access.role keyed by state id (sid) -> role => {grant_view, grant_update, grant_delete}. Conflict priority is workflow_access.settings:workflow_access_priority (default 0). Fixtures build a namespaced workflow 'wa_wf' (raw config, integer weights) and read/write workflow_access.role for its states; content_editor and anonymous are real roles on this site. All fixtures are torn down and the priority restored to 0.

evals.prompt: What does the Workflow Access submodule do, and what is its major limitation regarding entity types?
evals.expected_output: It controls access to content per workflow state and role (view/update/delete) through Drupal's node grant system. Because it uses node_access, it only works for node entities (one workflow per entity type).

evals.prompt: In Workflow Access, where do I set which roles can view/update/delete content in each workflow state, and in which config object are those grants stored?
evals.expected_output: On each workflow's Access tab (/admin/config/workflow/workflow/{workflow_type}/access) you tick view/update/delete per state and role. Grants are stored in the config object workflow_access.role, keyed by state id, as role => {grant_view, grant_update, grant_delete}.

evals.prompt: Other node access modules conflict with Workflow Access on my site. Which setting does Workflow Access provide to resolve that, and where is it?
evals.expected_output: The workflow_access_priority setting (config workflow_access.settings), set at /admin/config/workflow/workflow/access, controls the node-grant priority so Workflow Access can win or yield against other node-access modules.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the workflow 'wa_wf' has a 'Needs Review' state (wa_wf_review) with Workflow Access grants configured. Inspect the live configuration and state which role is allowed to edit (update) content in that state.
evals.expected_output: In workflow_access.role, the wa_wf_review key grants the content_editor role grant_view and grant_update, so content_editor can edit content in the Needs Review state.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the Workflow Access configuration and report the current node-grant priority value it is set to.

On this Drupal site there is a workflow 'wa_wf' with a 'Needs Review' state (state id wa_wf_review). Using Workflow Access, grant the 'content_editor' role both view and update access to content in that state, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In config workflow_access.role, the wa_wf_review key grants content_editor grant_view=1 and grant_update=1 (e.g. via the workflow's Access tab, or WorkflowAccessState('wa_wf_review')->insertAccess(['content_editor'=>['grant_view'=>1,'grant_update'=>1,'grant_delete'=>0]])).

evals.prompt: On this site there is a workflow 'wa_wf' with a Published state (state id wa_wf_published). I want anonymous visitors to be able to view content once it reaches the Published state. Set that up with Workflow Access on the live site.
evals.expected_output: In config workflow_access.role, the wa_wf_published key grants the anonymous role grant_view (via the workflow's Access tab or WorkflowAccessState('wa_wf_published')->insertAccess(['anonymous'=>['grant_view'=>1,...]])).
